conditions.name: Tension-type headache

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: The commonest headache: a dull, pressing band around the head, mild to moderate, with no nausea and no aversion to light, and not made worse by walking about.
workup: Simple analgesia, limited to avoid rebound

exam.positive: Score stratifies severity and tracks response

exam.step: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts, plans and means

conditions.name: Depression

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Persistent low mood and loss of interest for at least two weeks, with disturbed sleep, appetite, energy and concentration, and often guilt or hopelessness.
workup: Always ask directly about suicidal thoughts
TFTs, FBC, B12, vitamin D to exclude mimics

exam.step: Ask about caffeine, alcohol and stimulants

conditions.name: Generalised anxiety disorder

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Excessive, hard-to-control worry across many areas for six months or more, with restlessness, muscle tension, poor sleep and physical symptoms like palpitations.
workup: TFTs and ECG if physical symptoms prominent

exam.positive: Mild diffuse tenderness with no mass

exam.step: Check for abdominal mass or organomegaly
exam.positive: Their absence supports a functional disorder
Weight loss is a red flag against this diagnosis

labs.confirms: Normal distinguishes IBS from inflammatory bowel disease

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: A disorder of gut-brain interaction. Recurrent cramping with bloating and a changeable bowel habit, relieved by opening the bowels, going on for months without weight loss.
workup: FBC, CRP, coeliac serology, faecal calprotectin

exam.step: Observe during an attack if possible

conditions.name: Panic attack / panic disorder

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: A surge of intense fear peaking within minutes, with racing heart, breathlessness and tingling. Real and frightening, and a diagnosis of exclusion when cardiac risk exists.

exam.positive: An occasional dropped or early beat on a regular background
Ectopics that vanish with exercise are reassuring

labs.test: Thyroid function, FBC, electrolytes including magnesium

conditions.name: Benign ectopic beats

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Extra beats felt as a thud, flutter or missed beat. Very common, usually harmless, and typically worse at rest or when tired, caffeinated or stressed.

exam.positive: Tenderness at multiple sites without synovitis
Absence of synovitis is essential to the diagnosis

exam.step: Screen for sleep disturbance and mood

labs.test: FBC, CRP, ESR, TFTs, CK, vitamin D
labs.confirms: All normal; abnormal results suggest another diagnosis

labs.test: Widespread Pain Index and Symptom Severity Scale

conditions.name: Fibromyalgia

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Widespread pain with unrefreshing sleep, fatigue and cognitive fog lasting months, with normal inflammatory markers and no joint swelling.
workup: FBC, CRP, TFTs, vitamin D, CK to exclude alternatives

exam.step: Palpate the thyroid and auscultate for a bruit
Test for a fine tremor with paper on outstretched hands

exam.positive: Lid lag, proptosis and ophthalmoplegia in Graves

labs.test: TSH, free T4 and free T3
labs.confirms: Suppressed TSH with raised free hormones

conditions.name: Hyperthyroidism
conditions.summary: An overactive thyroid speeding everything up: weight loss despite eating well, heat intolerance, tremor, palpitations, anxiety and loose stools.

exam.positive: Abrupt termination strongly supports a re-entrant tachycardia

labs.confirms: Narrow complex regular tachycardia, P waves often buried

conditions.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
conditions.summary: A sudden, regular, very fast rhythm arising above the ventricles. Starts and stops abruptly like a switch, often in otherwise healthy younger people.

exam.step: Assess airway for swelling and stridor

exam.positive: Urticaria and angioedema in most but not all

labs.confirms: Identifies the trigger and provides an action plan

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: A rapid, whole-body allergic reaction with airway swelling, wheeze and collapse, usually minutes after a food, sting or drug. Adrenaline first, everything else after.

exam.step: Ask specifically about intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours
exam.positive: Distinct from generalised worry -- obsessions and/or compulsions that consume significant time and cause distress
Obsessions involving harm to others plus a plan or intent need urgent psychiatric risk assessment

labs.confirms: Quantifies severity and monitors treatment response

conditions.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Intrusive, unwanted, distressing thoughts (obsessions) and/or repetitive behaviours performed to reduce the distress (compulsions), that consume significant time and impair functioning. Frequently misunderstood as simple 'worry' or a personality trait rather than a treatable condition. Obsessions with harm to others, plus a plan/intent, need urgent psychiatric risk assessment rather than being assumed to be 'just OCD'.
workup: Clinical diagnosis; standardised scales (e.g. Y-BOCS) can help quantify severity and monitor treatment response
CBT with exposure and response prevention is first-line
SSRIs (often at higher doses than for depression) as an adjunct or alternative

exam.step: Ask directly about intrusive memories/flashbacks, nightmares, avoidance of trauma reminders, and feeling constantly 'on edge'
exam.positive: The actual diagnostic hallmarks of PTSD -- none of these have a dedicated evidence node in this checker, a significant, disclosed limitation

exam.step: Establish the timing: symptoms following a specific traumatic event, persisting beyond one month
exam.positive: The defining temporal and causal pattern required for diagnosis

exam.step: Screen for depression, substance use, and self-harm risk
exam.positive: Genuinely common comorbidities that need their own direct assessment, not assumed from anxiety symptoms alone

labs.test: Clinical diagnostic interview against DSM-5/ICD-11 criteria
labs.confirms: The actual basis for diagnosis -- there is no laboratory or imaging test for PTSD

labs.test: Referral to a mental health specialist
labs.confirms: For structured assessment and access to trauma-focused psychotherapy

conditions.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Arrange an appointment in the next day or two

conditions.summary: Persistent anxiety, sleep disturbance and low mood developing after exposure to a traumatic event, lasting more than a month. DISCLOSED SIGNIFICANT LIMITATION: no evidence node anywhere in this checker captures the actual diagnostic hallmarks of PTSD -- intrusive flashbacks/re-experiencing, hypervigilance, avoidance of trauma reminders, or a specific history of traumatic exposure. This condition is modelled here only through generic anxiety-cluster symptom overlap, a genuine, honestly-disclosed gap rather than a confident diagnostic tool for this specific condition -- always ask directly about a trauma history and the specific re-experiencing/avoidance/hypervigilance symptoms in practice, which this checker cannot substitute for.
workup: Ask directly about a specific traumatic event and the timing of symptom onset relative to it -- no evidence node captures this directly here
Trauma-focused psychotherapy (trauma-focused CBT, EMDR) -- genuinely the first-line, most effective treatment, not medication alone
Medication (certain antidepressants) can help alongside therapy, particularly for associated depression/anxiety, but is not the primary treatment
Screen for safety concerns (self-harm risk, substance use as a coping mechanism) given genuine comorbidity

redFlags.label: Possible sepsis
redFlags.message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

redFlags.label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
redFlags.message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.

redFlags.label: Possible severe allergic reaction
redFlags.message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
redFlags.action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

redFlags.label: Reduced consciousness
redFlags.message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

redFlags.label: Possible stroke
redFlags.message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

redFlags.label: Seizure
redFlags.message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
redFlags.action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

redFlags.label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
redFlags.message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
redFlags.action: Go to an emergency department now.

redFlags.label: New jaundice
redFlags.message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.

redFlags.label: Sudden loss of vision
redFlags.message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

redFlags.label: Thoughts of self-harm
redFlags.message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
redFlags.action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

redFlags.label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
redFlags.message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

disclaimer: This tool provides information about possible causes of symptoms. It is not a diagnosis and it cannot examine you. It does not replace assessment by a qualified clinician. If you feel very unwell, or your symptoms are getting rapidly worse, seek medical help immediately regardless of what this tool says.
